title: Lesson 4: Prompting for Agents: System Prompts, Few-Shot, and When Prompts Aren't Enough
description: In an agent, the prompt isn't a single message; it's the constitution the loop obeys on every iteration. The anatomy of a production system prompt, how few-shot examples actually work, and the escalation ladder for when words stop being enough.

questions.question: What is the role of a system prompt in an agent?
options: A one-time instruction sent only on the very first turn
The persistent instruction block used on every turn
A fallback used only when the model fails
An optional courtesy message shown to the user
questions.explanation: Because the loop re-sends it on each turn, the system prompt acts as the agent's constitution: the durable role, rules, and output format it obeys throughout.

questions.question: A model keeps producing worse output as more instructions are added to the prompt. What does this reflect?
options: Each added token depletes a finite attention budget and degrades recall
The model runs out of storage space for new instructions once the prompt grows long
The prompt text is being translated into another language
The system has exceeded its provider rate limit
questions.explanation: Recall falls as the context fills, so redundant context spends attention that the model needs for the actual task.

questions.question: A model cannot emit the required output format no matter how the prompt is reworded. What does this indicate?
options: A knowledge gap that retrieval would fix
A behavior gap that fine-tuning would fix
A reliability gap that a deterministic workflow gate would fix
A capability gap that only a different model fixes
questions.explanation: No wording change can supply a token sequence the model cannot produce, so an inability to emit a format is a capability gap answered by model selection or enforced output.
